model_boundary: pkg12_space_01021300 is modeled as the live zero-argument global-state wrapper. It reads the host stand-ins g_simulator_space_player_data and g_simulator_empire_lookup, then calls refresh_player_empire_staged. The staged helper is not claimed to be the exact entry point; it exposes the live pre-staged four-byte ID word and lookup boundary without recreating the shared map type.

live_abi.return_observation: The return is the cached pointer at sSpacePlayerData+0x1c, or zero when the empire key is 0xffffffff. No return-path AddRef is present.

lookup_interface.root: FUN_00B3D2A0 at 0x00B3D2A0 returns DAT_0167EAE4 in EAX and has no formal arguments; the live body has already staged the empire ID on the caller stack
lookup_interface.find: FUN_00BA9370 at 0x00BA9370 is __thiscall, receives the root object in ECX and consumes the staged empire ID from the caller stack with RET 4, and returns a pointer word
lookup_interface.model_shape: EmpireLookup contains RootWithStagedId and FindWithStagedId callbacks; both receive the four-byte StagedIdWord so the host model exposes the machine path without claiming a formal argument on the live root getter

staged_id_word.live_path: PUSH EAX precedes the no-argument root getter, then the same stack word is consumed by FUN_00BA9370
staged_id_word.model_path: refresh_player_empire_staged creates one StagedIdWord and passes it to RootWithStagedId and FindWithStagedId
staged_id_word.entry_boundary: refresh_player_empire_staged is a testable machine-boundary model, not the live zero-argument entry

lookup_interface.shared_map_policy: No map or map entry type is duplicated; the callback boundary preserves only the root and find operations required by this body

mechanics: The live zero-argument entry reads the global state pointer and dispatches to the staged-ID model boundary.
The staged model creates one four-byte StagedIdWord from the global cache+0x18 field before the sentinel check.
Return null immediately for staged_id.value == 0xffffffff, preserving the old cache and all reference counts.
Read old_empire from cache+0x1c; accept it without a lookup when it is non-null and empire+0x84 equals staged_id.value.
On refresh, pass the same StagedIdWord to the root boundary first, then pass it to the thiscall find boundary with the root.
If the lookup result equals old_empire, leave the cache unchanged and do not call AddRef or Release.
If the lookup result is distinct and non-null, AddRef it before storing it at cache+0x1c.
After the store, Release old_empire when it is non-null.
Return cache+0x1c without AddRef; the returned empire is borrowed from the cache.

state_cases.name: distinct_refresh
state_cases.condition: lookup returns a pointer different from old_empire

state_cases.name: null_lookup
state_cases.condition: lookup returns null and old_empire is non-null

state_global.name: Simulator::sSpacePlayerData
state_global.observed_initialization: FUN_01021D40 allocates 0x34 bytes, writes +0x18 and +0x1c, and stores the pointer at 0x016DDA8C

evidence.observation: The live function has no parameters, body range 0x01021300 through 0x01021368, and undefined return type.
The decompiler shows the +0x18 sentinel check, +0x84 identity check, root lookup, distinct-pointer AddRef, cache store, old-pointer Release, and cached return.

The exact 43-instruction body compares EAX with -1, reads [ECX+0x84], calls 0x00B3D2A0 and 0x00BA9370, invokes vtable slot 0 on a distinct new pointer, stores it, invokes vtable slot 1 on the old pointer, and returns [global+0x1c].
The live body is 105 bytes; the bytes confirm CMP EAX,-1, the +0x84 load, the two calls, the two indirect vtable calls, and the two return paths.
Only FUN_00B3D2A0 and FUN_00BA9370 are direct callees.
The live function has 182 direct caller functions.
The live function has 299 xrefs, including calls from FUN_0102D1B0, FUN_01021370, and FUN_0102DF20.
The root getter returns DAT_0167EAE4 with no arguments; the lookup helper rejects -1, searches its shared map through the thiscall boundary, and returns the stored intrusive pointer word.
SpacePlayerData exposes +0x18 mPlayerEmpireID and +0x1c mpPlayerEmpire; cEmpire exposes the compared raw word at +0x84.
Initialization allocates the 0x34-byte state, writes 0xffffffff to +0x18, writes zero to +0x1c, and publishes the state pointer at 0x016DDA8C.
The live global is named Simulator::sSpacePlayerData and has 56 xrefs; its documentation state is incomplete in Ghidra but its field accesses are directly observed.

confidence.shared_map_storage: medium; consumed through the existing lookup boundary
confidence.empire_identity_semantics: medium-low; the compared field is labeled mTrait in Ghidra

verification.layout_check: The model static_asserts SpacePlayerCache offsets 0x18 and 0x1c and Empire identity offset 0x84.

unresolved_questions: The shared map owner and concrete manager type behind DAT_0167EAE4 and FUN_00BA9370 remain outside this package.
The semantic name of cEmpire+0x84 is unresolved; Ghidra labels it mTrait while the target treats it as the cache identity word.

The live cache validates only the existing cached empire's +0x84 identity before refresh and does not validate a newly returned empire's +0x84 identity after 0x00ba9370. Because 0x00ba9370 is guarded-hybrid dependent, its result can be null/anchor or a nonmatching empire, so the live body may AddRef/store a nonmatching new pointer without an identity check.
The 182 callers establish broad use but do not by themselves establish a universal ownership contract beyond the observed cache AddRef/store/Release behavior.
The host globals are explicit stand-ins for the live global at 0x016DDA8C and the lookup boundary; they are not linked to integrated PKG-12 source in this assignment.
The live root getter has no formal staged-ID argument; RootWithStagedId is intentionally a host adapter that exposes the pre-existing stack word for the model.
blockers: A native integration test against the original global state is not available without modifying the existing PKG-12 integration boundary, which is out of scope.
The lookup interface is modeled at the root and thiscall find boundaries; no shared map type or runtime manager allocation is reconstructed here.
The borrowed return is preserved by the absence of a return-path AddRef, but concrete cEmpire vtable ownership remains unresolved.
